_comment: Benchmark floors for the verification loop. `pnpm verify` fails when the engine's PIG test-split scores drop below `engine`, when its lint errors per 1000 notes rise above `lint.errorsPer1000Max`, or when a gated run skips a piece. Raise the floor when a milestone improves the numbers; never lower it without a dated note in docs/PROGRESS.md. All numbers are percent, macro-averaged over the test pieces. 2026-10-14: `engine`, `textbook` and `lint` are the M2 rule-based floors (Parncutt + Jacobs + Balliauw rules, hand-position term, textbook templates, literature-default weights, profile large), first set from the m2-rules scorecard (macro gen 59.74, high 66.02, soft 80.28, rec 70.05). 2026-10-14 (M2 review fixes: held-note loop that keeps one side of each conflict, doubled-finger cost for chords of more than five notes, hop weight 10 with 2 points for a hop within a fourth at any tempo, chordBeyondPractical 30, lint L05 a law only on keys held together): raised from the m2-rules-fixed scorecard on 42c24fc plus the uncommitted fix tree (macro gen 60.91, high 66.84, soft 81.65, rec 71.46 over 30 test pieces, 0 skipped) minus 0.5 and rounded down to one decimal. 2026-10-14 (M2 hardening, docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-14-m2-hardening.md: every pair of a chord priced and the chord law infinite where a slice has a legal configuration, notated holds beyond reach released, melodic beyondPractical waived after a rest or a release and on thumb crossings within a fourth, chromatic runs templated; lint checks every held pair): `engine` raised from the m2-hardened scorecard on 4dbf87b plus the uncommitted hardening tree (macro gen 61.60, high 67.59, soft 82.38, rec 72.26 over 30 test pieces, 0 skipped) minus 0.5 and rounded down to one decimal; `textbook` raised; `lint` re-based on the stricter lint (see its note). Still 0.5 below nakamura_chmm on gen: the verification spec's gen gate (the best runnable baseline, 62.1) is not met by the rules alone; see docs/experiments.md and benchmarks/history.md. 2026-10-14 (M2 hardening re-review fixes, label m2-hardened-fixed: a key held under a later note is a law at any distance, priced like a chord partner by the decoder for the two nearest notes, by a law-domain pass (arc consistency) and the held-note loop beyond; solver and lint walk the same holds (reach.ts forEachHold); a chord with no legal configuration breaks the fewest pairs; the doubled finger of a slice of more than five notes is the named rule doubledFinger): `engine` raised from the m2-hardened-fixed scorecard on 4dbf87b plus the uncommitted tree (macro gen 61.89, high 67.93, soft 82.62, rec 72.56 over 30 test pieces, 0 skipped) minus 0.5 and rounded down to one decimal; `textbook` unchanged (same measurement); `lint.errorsPer1000Max` lowered from 12.43 to 3.82, the new measurement rounded up, below the 8.32 it had before the hardening re-based it (see its note). Still 0.2 below nakamura_chmm on gen (62.1). 2026-10-14 (M3 Task 5): weightSet names the weight set every floor here was measured with; bench gates a run against these floors only with that set (another set is a breach), and pnpm verify passes it as --weights. It stays parncutt until M3 Task 9 re-bases the floors on learned-open (both learned sets score 3.91 lint errors per 1000 test notes, above the 3.82 gate). mutopia is the held-out Mutopia oracle (the test half of research/data/splits/mutopia_split.json, gold notes without a finger masked): pnpm verify scores it as the step benchmark:mutopia and writes benchmarks/latest-mutopia.json; its gen floor is null (reported, not gated) until M3 Task 9 sets it. 2026-10-14 (M3 Task 9): the floors are re-based on the shipped learned set, weightSet learned-open (RECOMMENDED_WEIGHT_SET, fitted on the textbook oracle, Beringer and the Mutopia train half only), whose weights hash weightSetHash 7ba9363fea541a4e is recorded beside it: bench treats another set or another hash under the same name as a breach. Measured by the labelled runs m3-open (PIG test, 30 pieces, 0 skipped: macro gen 63.89, high 70.48, soft 85.27, rec 76.37, lint 3.912 errors per 1000, calibration ECE 0.0684 per annotator at temperature 3.071694) and mutopia-open (Mutopia test half, 62 parts, 0 skipped: gen 65.48), on 4dcf9c2 plus the uncommitted M3 tree; scorecards benchmarks/latest.json and benchmarks/latest-mutopia.json. `engine` and `mutopia.gen` are the measurements minus 0.5, rounded down to one decimal, all above the parncutt floors they replace (61.3, 67.4, 82.1, 72.0; mutopia was null). `calibration.eceMax` is new (see its note). `lint.errorsPer1000Max` is the one maximum loosened, under forced-error evidence (see its note). bench picks the block a run is gated by from the run's split file (`split` here for engine, lint and calibration; `mutopia.split` for mutopia), not from the split's free-text dataset field. pnpm verify writes its scorecards to the gitignored benchmarks/runs/verify-pig.json and verify-mutopia.json; only labelled milestone runs replace benchmarks/latest.json and latest-mutopia.json (docs/verification-loop.md). The textbook floors below stay those of the solver's own default set (parncutt), which textbook.test.ts solves with.

mutopia.note: Held-out Mutopia oracle, editorial fingerings of the test half (62 parts of 48 pieces), gold notes without a finger masked (8,805 of 56,937 notes scored). 2026-10-14 M3 Task 9: gen 64.9 = mutopia-open 65.48 minus 0.5, rounded down (parncutt scores 61.15 on the same parts with the same engine). Calibration on these parts is reported, not gated: ECE 0.1037 at the learned-open temperature fitted on PIG validation (mean confidence 0.579 against mean accuracy 0.657: the editors agree with the engine more often than its PIG-fitted confidence says).

calibration.note: Largest expected calibration error (a fraction) of the per-note confidence on the PIG test split with weightSet; bench gates it with the engine block. Correctness is per annotator (M3 Task 9; verification spec 3.8): a bucket's accuracy is the mean share of a note's annotators who use the engine's finger, so the measure does not depend on the number of annotators per piece (validation 1.2, test 5). 2026-10-14 m3-open: ECE 0.06841 over 10,225 notes at temperature 3.071694 (fitted on the PIG validation notes only; validation ECE 0.0517); eceMax = measured + 0.02, rounded up to four decimals, under the goals table's floor of 0.10 (target 0.05). Under Task 6's any-annotator definition the same set had scored 0.243 on test against 0.063 on validation. The research set learned-pig scores 0.0451 (m3-pig, not shipped).

textbook.note: Fractions, not percent: textbook oracle (benchmarks/textbook, 672 entries) note accuracy, measured minus 0.01 and rounded down to two decimals. noteAccuracy, scaleNoteAccuracy and quarter are at quarter = 120 (IOI 0.5 s, the evaluateTextbook default); sixteenths at qpm 480 (IOI 0.125 s); R and L are each hand's entries alone, which guard the left-hand mirror. packages/engine/src/eval/textbook.test.ts reads these values and enforces them in the unit step. 2026-10-14 m2-rules: quarter note 0.527, scale 0.552 (exact 29 of 672). 2026-10-14 m2-rules-fixed: quarter note 0.8422, scale 0.9143, arpeggio 0.7334, chromatic 0.6283, right hand 0.8731, left hand 0.8112 (exact 410 of 672: scales 330 of 432, arpeggios 80 of 192, chromatic 0 of 48); sixteenths identical, since a hop within a fourth now costs the same at any tempo. 2026-10-14 m2-hardened: quarter note 0.8802, scale 0.9143, arpeggio 0.7737, chromatic 1.0000, right hand 0.9227, left hand 0.8377 (exact 486 of 672: scales 330 of 432, arpeggios 108 of 192, chromatic 48 of 48; right hand 257 of 336, left hand 229 of 336, left-hand arpeggios 46 of 96 the weakest group at note accuracy 0.6505); sixteenths identical. 2026-10-14 m2-hardened-fixed: unchanged at both tempos (exact 486 of 672, note accuracy 0.8802); the oracle's melodies never hold a key under a later note, so the held-pair law does not touch them.

lint.note: Lint errors per 1000 notes of the solver's output on the 30 test pieces; bench gates it. 2026-10-14 M3 Task 9 (weightSet learned-open): 3.92 = the m3-open measurement 3.912 (40 errors in 10,225 notes) rounded up to two decimals, the rule M2 used for 3.82 (no slack: with bench's 0.005 tolerance 40 errors pass and 41, 4.010 per 1000, fail); the one maximum loosened, from 3.82, under the coordinator's rule that it may loosen only when the extra errors are forced. Evidence: the one error learned-open has beyond parncutt's 39 is in piece 029 (25 against 24; pieces 025 1, 026 14, 029 25, every other piece 0, the same as parncutt), the piece whose hard decode M2 found infeasible (legato overlaps of 9 to 27 ms; docs/PROGRESS.md, M2 Task 11 entry; not re-analysed here, the test split is only scored); and on the 20 validation pieces (M3 Task 7, docs/research/hard-errors-m3.md, an exact minimum-violation programme per hand) every law error of all three sets lies in the 9 hands that have no legal fingering, while each of the 31 hands with a legal fingering gets one from every set (learned-open 98, parncutt 97, exact minimum 94; learned-open's extra error is in 038 L, a hand of chords wider than the hand). No law error where a legal fingering exists, so no solver defect blocks the switch to learned-open; the excess over the exact minimum inside infeasible hands is the law pass's drop rule, shared by every set (a lead for the solver, not a lint gap). History: 2026-10-14 m2-rules 22.11 (226 errors, mostly L05 leaps between notes that do not overlap, which lint then called a law); m2-rules-fixed 8.313 (85 errors: L05 74, of them 68 chord spans, and L03 11; that note blamed the chord spans on PIG legato overlaps, the M2 review found the cause in the solver, which priced chord spans only between neighbouring notes of a slice). m2-hardened 12.42 (127 errors) under a stricter lint that checks every key still held against every later note it sounds with: 0 chord-span L05 where a legal configuration exists, but 98 held-pair L05, because the solver had no span law between a held key and a note other than its sequence neighbour; the gate was re-based to 12.43 for that run, which the re-review rejected (it hid avoidable solver errors). 2026-10-14 m2-hardened-fixed (gate 3.82, the measurement rounded up, under the same stricter lint): 39 errors in 10,225 notes, 3.81 per 1000; 0 relaxed hands; 7 slices with no legal configuration. The solver now treats a held key like a chord partner: the decoder charges the held-note penalty for a span beyond practical (or the same finger) between a note and a key held one or two steps back, a law-domain pass (arc consistency over every held pair and chord pair) forbids from the start the fingers no law-keeping fingering can use, and the held-note loop mends the rest. Breakdown: L05 22 = 14 chord spans, all inside the 7 infeasible slices, and 8 held pairs (98 before); L03 17 (15 before), 11 of them on a note of a chord, where more keys sound than the hand has fingers within reach. The experts' own fingerings of the test pieces (every annotator, 4 to 6 per piece, 50,014 notes) score 8.00 errors per 1000 notes under this lint (L03 4.36, L05 3.12, L01 0.48, L02 0.04; 6.68 under the m2-rules-fixed lint, 47.4 under the m2-rules lint).

hands.note: Hand separation (digitus2 evalhands): macro accuracy in percent on the PIG test split, first annotation of each piece, channel = truth. Set by M6 Task 9 to the measured value minus 1.0. Set 2026-10-14 by M6 Task 9 from 92.05 (commit 86ea924, measured on the uncommitted M6 Tasks 3-6 tree over it; label m6-hands; macro 92.0499 minus 1.0, rounded down to one decimal; note-weighted 91.89; shipped tables from the library and the Mutopia train half, no PIG data).

embellish.note: Light embellishment ("Add notes between", docs/research/embellishment-spike.md section 6): the pieces at levels 1 and 2 that the guard offers (packages/engine/src/embellish/guard.ts: the light embellisher, the independent check, then solve with learned-open at the large, medium, small and child profiles and lint with beginner: true; zero law errors and no more beginner errors than the plain score at every profile, the figures of offending bars dropped once, at least three figures). digitus2 embellish --library also fails on any offered piece whose independent check, lint or level proposal (at most one up) fails. offeredMin is the measured count: the run is deterministic, so a drop is a change to explain, not noise. Measured 175 of 267 (794 passing and 346 neighbour notes, 13 offered after the retry, 20 retried).

nakamura_chmm.note: Nakamura's released combined HMM on the official PIG test split (30 pieces), measured by the baselines agent on 2026-10-13 with the Python scorer that matches the official C++ evaluator to 5e-7

human_agreement_ceiling.note: inter-annotator general match rate reported by Nakamura et al. 2020; re-measured in docs/research/datasets.md
